title: The Root Edit Primitive is deployed only once yet stays Active, making its single Instance a standing governance channel
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.1.4 and A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.4 both state that "because the Root Edit Primitive is deployed only once, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked" — the same closing language used for the Genesis Primitives. Yet its Global Activation Status (A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.1.1) is `Active`, not `Completed`, and its single Instance sits in the Active Instances directory.

The contrast disambiguates two things the Hub structure otherwise conflates. "One Instance only" is a statement about how many configurations of the Primitive can exist; `Active` versus `Completed` is a statement about whether that configuration is still doing work. Genesis Primitives are both single-Instance and finished. Root Edit is single-Instance and permanent.

This is why the Root Edit Instance is the only one in the Osero Artifact whose Parameters document defers entirely to process: A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.1 states that "the parameters of the Root Edit Primitive are fully specified by the Operational Process Definition." A standing channel has no configuration values to record — its content *is* its protocol.

The reading rule that follows is practical: to know whether a Primitive is live machinery or a completed historical act, read the Global Activation Status, not the Invocation prohibition.
description: Unlike Genesis Primitives that close after completing, this one-shot deployment remains permanently `Active` — Instance count and process usage are separate dimensions.
